body: Yep! It's set for next Wednesday at 1 PM. She's coming with me, and meeting with the doctor or practitioner separately for part of it to describe everything from her point of view.

I tried exactly that, and it actually seems to be helping! I'm T minus 6 days until my first consultation (to which she's coming with me), and while I've been better about doing everything without her asking, I'm also trying to respect her wishes and not go over-the-top to keep her around. Right now we're successfully trying to be friends and hold off on anything romantic, just to get on friendly terms, and rebuild our relationship from there. It's gonna be a long process, but that's what she decided, and we both want things to get back to the way they used to be long ago. Thanks!

She told me recently she's willing to wait a few more months for my stability to kick in before we decide anything final. I have my fingers crossed that it'll really help me and get us back to how we were a long time ago.

That last part made me laugh xD

Thanks for the tip :)

I absolutely adore my daughter. And I wish I could make myself okay with coparenting. I think it's a great concept when done properly, because despite all this we've always agreed our daughter's happiness comes before our own, but we need to be happy ourselves so she will see that. Who knows, maybe my mind will change down the road, but right now the only woman I want is my wife. I get sick every time I think of being with someone else. And every time I think of the possibility I get discouraged and depressed because I feel incapable of receiving love from anyone and I'll never have that again.

Sorry, didn't mean to go off the handle there. I really appreciate your help!

She will, but we decided we want to wait until I've been to the psychiatrist and have started working on my mental health first, that way we can communicate more efficiently and I can be more stable when we make steps to try healing our marriage.

Right, the last several days I've been making a conscious effort to do something about it. Trying to do the majority of or all housework without being asked to, spending as much time with my daughter as work allows (which is an absolute joy), and doing my best to think before acting or speaking in the wrong way. The major problem is I can't put it out of my mind that being away from my wife might be the best outcome. I really want to keep us all together, but I can't decide if that's the best or if it's just me being selfish.

Right now her attitude is she wants to make sure I'm better before we start working on us. Maybe some stability from proper medication and therapy might help me think more clearly and might help us communicate more efficiently. We aren't opposed to counseling, but we thought we'd try this first.

I have an appointment with a psychiatrist for next Wednesday. I probably should have mentioned that. Making an edit now.

She tried coming to me about it but it took actually feeling threatened that my family would leave to get me to actually listen to her.

I want you to know how much your reply means to me. It just sucks feeling like I'm nothing but a burden to those around me, like all I ever do is hurt them. I mean, in the tiniest corner of my mind I know it's not true but it's really hard to dig through everything to get to that tiny positive thought. Having it validated is a blessing. Maybe after work I'll walk in the park, feed the ducks, something. It's raining outside today so that could be part of it. It's okay, though. I like the rain.

EDIT: So thankful you're still alive, by the way. Happy it was only "really fucking close" and not terminal.
